clue.text: False god with middle name that's commonplace

indicators.note: the false god is given a middle letter, so the name abbreviation sits at its centre

parts.note: Baal is the Canaanite deity condemned in the Bible as a false god

explanation.surface: A pagan idol with an unremarkable middle name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with middle' puts N inside BAAL, splitting it BA-AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something ordinary and unoriginal, lacking any freshness.

clue.text: Cloak for man in the New Testament

indicators.note: the testament abbreviation is set within the word for a man

parts.note: a man is a male
NT is the usual abbreviation for the New Testament

explanation.surface: Asking what garment a man in the Gospels might wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's order is loose: 'in' really means the man takes the testament in, the man being the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A long sleeveless outer garment or cape is a synonym for a cloak.

clue.text: Idealistic campaigner

parts.note: someone fighting passionately for a cause, named after the medieval holy warriors of the Holy Land expeditions

explanation.definitionFit: A zealous reformer is called by the name once given to medieval holy warriors.

clue.text: Seems to be a notably soft fruit

parts.note: in musical notation p (piano) marks a soft passage
pears are a fruit

explanation.surface: Something that looks like a strikingly squashy fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notably' points to musical notes: soft is p for piano.
explanation.definitionFit: To look or come across as something is a synonym of seems.

clue.text: An expert confined by a painful complaint is no stop-at-home

indicators.note: the expert is held within the painful condition, the condition acting as container

parts.note: gout is a painful inflammation of the joints
taken as A
a dab, or dab hand, is an expert

explanation.surface: An expert laid up with a painful ailment can hardly be a homebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confined by' sets the expert inside the ailment. The irony is that gout would keep anyone at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone always out and about socially is the opposite of a person who stays indoors.

clue.text: Study for one with his head in the clouds…

definitions.text: Study for one with his head in the clouds…

parts.words: Study for one with his head in the clouds
parts.note: a dreamer is said to have his head in the clouds, but literally this is the science of studying clouds

explanation.definitionFit: The scientific study of clouds is named from the Greek word nephos, cloud.

clue.text: Fresh start for one after a long sentence

definitions.text: Fresh start for one after a long sentence

parts.words: Fresh start for one after a long sentence
parts.note: sounds like a released prisoner's new life, but it is a new block of text begun after a sentence

explanation.definitionFit: A new section of prose begins on a fresh line, often after lengthy sentences.

clue.text: Finally checked in a match

explanation.definitionFit: In chess a king finally checked with no escape is checkmated; a pair of animals or people joined in a match are paired up.

clue.text: … or on the pillow?

parts.note: continues the previous clue: someone whose head is on the pillow rather than in the clouds is lying in bed

explanation.definitionFit: Lying in bed with one's head on the pillow, an old word for being in bed.

clue.text: What the curate felt it would be to complain about his egg?

definitions.text: What the curate felt it would be to complain about his egg?

parts.words: What the curate felt it would be to complain about his egg
parts.note: the Punch cartoon curate, given a rotten egg by his bishop, said it was good in parts rather than complain

explanation.walkthrough: The 'curate's egg' is a famous Punch cartoon: a timid curate served a bad egg at the bishop's table says 'parts of it are excellent'. Complaining would have been impolite; the egg itself also tasted off.
explanation.definitionFit: Impoliteness or poor judgement in manners, and also the flavour of a rotten egg.

clue.text: Eminence could be a church day, he discovered

indicators.note: the words could be something else, a hint that their letters are to be rearranged
the letters, mixed, reveal a new name that he found

explanation.surface: A man stumbles on a high point while spending a day at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could' and 'discovered' signal an anagram of A CH DAY HE, giving ACHYHEAD after BE, which stays as written.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminence is a high piece of ground; this is a chalk headland on the Sussex coast of England.

clue.text: See 11
Birds electing places in Russia?

parts.note: red was the colour of Soviet Russia
polls are the places where people vote

explanation.surface: Asking where Russians go to vote.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' is a link: Russian voting booths would be red polls.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small finches with a crimson patch on the crown.

clue.text: Tinder-just for luck, say

explanation.definitionFit: Decayed dry wood used to kindle fire is tinder; people say the phrase to ward off bad luck.

clue.text: Many bids for a store of money

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, so many
bids are offers

explanation.surface: Lots of bids for a stockpile of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Strongboxes or a treasury hold an organisation's funds.

clue.text: Quick, yes, rounding the old copper; but they won't run

parts.note: quick means fast
d was the symbol for the old British penny, a copper coin

explanation.surface: A hurried 'yes' around a bygone policeman, who refuses to flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounding' puts D inside YES. 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is a pre-1971 British penny, written d.
explanation.definitionFit: Colourfast dyes do not bleed or spread when washed.

clue.text: Wise man takes a cut in payment to avoid the army in feudal times

definitions.text: payment to avoid the army in feudal times

indicators.note: the wise man takes in the cut, holding it inside

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
taken as cut

explanation.surface: A sage accepts a cut of a medieval levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' means the wise man takes in the cut. Scutage is a medieval English tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal tenant could pay this tax instead of doing military service for the lord.

clue.text: Antipathy shown to a swindler with charm

parts.note: a con, or con man, is a swindler
to charm or lure is to tempt

explanation.surface: Dislike felt toward a charming swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn or disdain is a strong feeling of dislike.

clue.text: Greek hero brought colour to America

parts.note: perse is a dark greyish-blue colour
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A Greek hero brought colour to the New World.
explanation.walkthrough: PERSE is a rare word for a dark blue-grey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero who slew Medusa.

clue.text: Slip along and freeze the fish

parts.note: to ice is to freeze
the skate is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Glide off and chill the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Gliding over a frozen surface on blades is slipping along.

clue.text: A river on the ebb in Italy

definitions.text: A river on the ebb in Italy

indicators.note: an ebb is a tide flowing back, so the little word on before it is turned around

explanation.surface: A river running low somewhere in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ebb' turns ON into NO; 'in Italy' completes the definition of the Tuscan river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuscan river flowing through Florence and Pisa.

clue.text: Time for reflection

indicators.note: a mirror reflection reads the same, so the answer reads identically backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A moment set aside for quiet thought.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads the same both ways, a reflection of itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday, twelve o'clock, is a time of day.

clue.text: Doesn't affect the port

indicators.note: to affect is to change something, so the letters of the first word are altered

explanation.surface: Something that leaves the harbour unmoved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affect' signals an anagram of DOESNT (apostrophe ignored).
explanation.definitionFit: A Belgian ferry port on the North Sea coast.

clue.text: Part of the service, I believe

explanation.definitionFit: A statement of faith recited in the church liturgy; its Latin first word credo means 'I believe'.

clue.text: Scandinavian corner of Paradise?

definitions.note: the adjective stands for a Scandinavian country

parts.note: SW, south-west, is a corner of a map
Eden was the paradise garden of Genesis

explanation.definitionFit: A Nordic kingdom bordering Norway and Finland.

clue.text: Observes sailors in a dazed condition

parts.note: observes means sees
tars is slang for sailors

explanation.definitionFit: After a blow to the head one is said to glimpse twinkling lights, being stunned.

clue.text: Protagonist in a dog-fight?

parts.note: a fighter in the ring, and also a breed of dog, so a dog that fights

explanation.definitionFit: A pugilist in a bout, and a dog breed, so a fighter that is a dog.

clue.text: Hold-up rather in the nature of a leg-pull

definitions.text: Hold-up rather in the nature of a leg-pull

parts.words: Hold-up rather in the nature of a leg-pull
parts.note: sounds like a robbery that is really a joke, but describes a garter strap that holds stockings up and pulls on the leg

explanation.definitionFit: A strap or garter that holds up socks or stockings by tugging on them.
